title: Medicare Card Scam Calls
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare, saying you need a new card or your benefits will stop. They ask for your Medicare number or other personal information.
example_message: "This is Medicare calling. We need to confirm your Medicare number to send you a new card. If you don’t give it, your coverage will be canceled."
red_flags: Pressure to give your Medicare number
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text saying a package couldn’t be delivered and you need to click a link to reschedule. The link leads to a fake website that tries to steal your information or install malware.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please confirm your address by clicking here: [fake link]"
red_flags: Requests for personal or payment info
what_to_do: Do not click the link. Delete the message and check with the delivery company using their official website.

title: Social Security Email Phishing
how_it_works: Scammers send emails that look like they’re from the Social Security Administration, saying there’s a problem with your account. They ask you to click a link and enter your Social Security number.
example_message: "We have detected suspicious activity on your Social Security account. Please verify your information here to avoid suspension."
red_flags: Email asks for your Social Security number
Links that don’t go to ssa.gov
what_to_do: Do not reply or click any links. Go to ssa.gov or call Social Security directly if you’re worried.

title: Facebook Marketplace Overpayment Scam
how_it_works: A scammer contacts you about something you’re selling online. They send a fake payment for more than the price and ask you to send back the extra money. Their payment is fake, so you lose the money you send.
example_message: "I accidentally sent you $200 instead of $100 for your item. Can you please send back the extra $100?"
red_flags: Buyer overpays and asks for refund
Payment doesn’t show up in your bank
what_to_do: Never send money back to someone who overpays online. Wait until your bank confirms the payment is real.

title: Tech Support Pop-Up Scam
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer saying you have a virus and must call a number for help. The person on the phone asks for remote access to your computer and may demand payment.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft support now at 1-800-XXX-XXXX."
red_flags: Phone number to call for help
Requests for remote access or payment
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number. If you’re worried, ask a trusted friend or take your computer to a local repair shop.
